newsitem.title: USA: Israel scandal not to derail peace effort -Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Israel scandal not to derail peace effort -Clinton.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Friday the crisis swirling about Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu must not be allowed to derail stalled Middle East peace efforts.

He said a police recommendation that Netanyahu be charged with fraud was "obviously an internal matter for Israel to deal with", adding: "They are a great and vibrant democracy and they'll deal with that in their way."
But he told reporters at a briefing in the White House: "We just can't allow anything, anything to derail the peace process and I don't believe we will."
Clinton said he had had no conversation with Netanyahu since the Israeli leader visited Washington April 7.

Clinton has been working to revive the Middle East peace process, which ground to a halt after Israel went ahead with a controversial housing project in Arab East Jerusalem, which prompted violent Palestinians protests.

Middle East mediator Dennis Ross managed to get Israeli and Palestinian security chiefs to meet to discuss cooperation during a mission to the region this week but was returning to Washington leaving major gaps between the two sides.

Clinton said it was vital to keep pressing ahead to bring the two sides together. "The important thing is we get this security cooperation up and going and then we just keep plugging ahead here," he said.
